answer: Like an ocean that admits ships only at set tides, an agent economy can resist Sybils with issuance windows. New identities are minted only in a short window each epoch, capped at a number, and each mint pays a fee that doubles every fifty registrations and is burned. One honest agent, a prism, passes through once at the base fee, while an attacker needing a thousand fake lantern identities must queue across many windows and pay escalating, unrecoverable burns for every extra identity. The cap makes flooding slow and the burn makes scale expensive.
